reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read Raamah's Dedan and Jokshan's Dedan as two distinct Arabian peoples that happen to share a recurring tribal name across the two genealogies.

discrepancy.connective: J. S. Vater pressed the recurrence the other way: because in both lists Dedan's brother is alike named Sheba, the pair looks like one tribe preserved in variant traditions, not two independent fathers.

skeptic.name: Johann Severin Vater
skeptic.attribution: Johann Severin Vater (d. 1826), Commentar über den Pentateuch (1802-1805)

excerpts.excerpt_text: the posterity of this man most probably settled in Arabia, and yet are to be distinguished from the Dedanim in Isa 21:13 who were Arabians also, but descended from Dedan the son of Jokshan, a son of Abraham by Keturah, Gen 25:3 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill explicitly distinguishes the Cushite Dedan (son of Raamah) from the Keturahite Dedan (son of Jokshan, Gen 25:3) as two different peoples — the core harmonization for this contradiction.

excerpts.excerpt_text: There seem to be three different people of this name mentioned in this chapter, and a fourth in Gen 25:3.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke states the same-name/different-persons principle for these recurring Arabian eponyms, expressly extending it to Gen 25:3 — the principle that dissolves the apparent contradiction.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Sheba and Dedan: Cp. 10:7. Abraham's descendants probably settled in these regions and became identified by their names, along with people of other lineage.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Tyndale links the two lists directly (Cp. 10:7) and supplies the eponym/settlement mechanism: Abraham's descendants took on regional names already borne by people of another lineage.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Genesis 10:7
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, distinguishing the Cushite Dedan (son of Raamah) from the Keturahite Dedan (son of Jokshan, Gen 25:3) as two distinct peoples sharing the name.
